newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Moldova votes in presidential election runoff.
newsitem.headline: Moldova votes in presidential election runoff.

text.p: Polling stations opened in Moldova at 8 a.m. (0600 GMT) on Sunday for the second round of the former Soviet republic's first contested presidential election.

Some 2.4 million voters have the chance to choose between President Mircea Snegur, who won 39 percent of the vote in the first round on November 17, and parliament chairman Petru Lucinschi, who came second two weeks ago with 28 percent.
Voting was slow in the first quarter of an hour of polling at Middle School No 37 in the centre of the capital Chisinau.
Opinion polls have suggested a close race but they have a poor track record in Moldova, a wedge-shaped country of 4.3 million people between Ukraine and Romania.

Snegur, president since independence from Moscow in 1991, has enlisted the backing of nationalists who favour closer ties with the Moldovan majority's ethnic kin in neighbouring Romania. He has pledged to speed up market reforms but wants greater constitutional powers over the government to do it.

Lucinschi, like Snegur a former senior communist party official in Soviet times, has the backing of Moldova's communists and much of the one-third Russian-speaking minority. He has presented himself as a social democrat.
Lucinschi has accused Snegur of planning to put pressure on the police to help him win.

After the Soviet Union collapsed, the 700,000-strong Dnestr region broke away from Moldova in 1990 fearing its mostly Russian-speaking residents could be reduced to second-rate citizens in a possible merger with Romania.
Hundreds died in a conflict in 1992 which was ended by Russian troops, 6,000 of whom are still in the Dnestr region.
Lucinschi advocates openness to the West but wants close ties with Russia, Moldova's main supplier of fuel and energy.
Snegur has been at pains not to alienate the Russian-speaking minority. "No one is talking today about a merger with Romania," he said in a radio broadcast on Saturday.
